sentences.text: Clients receive a laminated card after each visit noting water parameters, livestock condition, and any recommended equipment upgrades. "Low on frozen mysis again — remind me to hit the wholesaler before Friday's route." Honestly, the hardest part of this job is parallel parking a van full of sloshing water jugs downtown. "Did the yellow one die?" asked the accountant, and I explained the wrasse was just sleeping under the sand. At the chiropractor's, the heater had drifted two degrees, so I swapped it rather than trust it another week. Every Monday begins the same way: load the siphon hoses, check the test kit expiry dates, coffee, then the freeway. Inside the van it smells permanently of brine, damp towels, and the vinyl gloves I buy in bulk. Why does every lobby aquarium end up positioned in direct afternoon sun? Next week I'll drain a third of the cichlid display at the credit union and finally rehome that bullying jewelfish. Nitrates were creeping past forty at the dental office, so I doubled the water change and made a note to recheck Thursday. Between the law firm and the pediatric clinic there's a twenty-minute gap he uses to refill carboys at the shop's RO station. We chatted about his daughter's soccer season while the gravel vacuum churned and the water level dropped inch by inch. Who decided a six-foot reef display belonged directly above the bank lobby's only electrical outlet? Meridian Dental's protein skimmer had overflowed onto the carpet, and the office manager greeted me holding a mop and a look. "Your clownfish keeps spitting sand at the powerhead," the receptionist told me, delighted, before I'd even set down my bucket. Salt creep had crusted the light fixture like frost, flaking onto my sleeve as I lifted the hood. Per the service agreement, filter media replacement at the Hartwell building occurs on the second Tuesday of each month. She's kneeling behind the reception desk, tracing an airline back to a pump somebody unplugged to charge a phone. You learn to knock before wheeling the cart through a lobby at 7 a.m., because somebody is always mid-meeting behind the glass wall. By the time she reached the insurance office, the algae on the back glass had thickened into green felt. You can smell the linseed oil before you even round the corner into the armor gallery. What is the meaning of the word tank?
